The last 7 permanent Stoke City managers ranked from worst to best

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1418 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since relegation from the Premier League in 2018, Stoke City have had seven different permanent managers/head coaches, and it would be a fair assessment to say that some have done better than others.
  • 2016 was the last time Stoke recorded a top-half finish of any division they have been in, with three ninth-placed finishes in a row in the Premier League being followed up by a decade of mediocrity and disappointment.
  • Right now, the Potters are flying towards the top of the league, and there is genuine hope amongst the fanbase that they can finally end their barren run this year and in style.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since relegation from the Premier League in 2018, Stoke City have had seven different permanent managers/head coaches, and it would be a fair assessment to say that some have done better than others.

2016 was the last time Stoke recorded a top-half finish of any division they have been in, with three ninth-placed finishes in a row in the Premier League being followed up by a decade of mediocrity and disappointment.

Right now, the Potters are flying towards the top of the league, and there is genuine hope amongst the fanbase that they can finally end their barren run this year and in style.

Stoke supporters have seen nearly everything since their relegation to the Championship, as Football League World has attempted to rank the last seven Potters managers from worst to best.

Kicking us off and the worst out of the bunch, although some will argue otherwise, is Nathan Jones.

Jones found success in his early days of management with Luton Town, helping to take the Hatters from League Two to League One, implementing his infamous 'diamond' formation, and with the Hatters flying high in the third tier in January 2019, he was poached by the Potters.

His time at the club, to put it bluntly, was horrific, losing his first two games in charge to Brentford and Shrewsbury Town, and guiding the club to a 16th-placed finish in their first year back in the Championship, as well as spending £7 million on Sam Vokes, then 29.

The free additions of the likes of Jordan Cousins, Lee Gregory, Nick Powell, Adam Davies, and Stephen Ward the following summer did little to excite supporters, and by the time November 2019 rolled around, he was dismissed with the Potters sitting at the foot of the second tier.

Six wins in 38 games managed, a win rate of just 15.79 percent, Jones is statistically the worst Stoke manager of all time to manage over 20 games, and whilst he has revived his career with Charlton Athletic, his time in the Potteries was an unmitigated disaster.

Just the third-ever manager Stoke have appointed that is from outside the British Isles, after Johan Boskamp and the late Gudjon Thordarson, Narcis Pelach arrived in North Staffordshire in September 2024 following the surprising dismissal of Steven Schumacher.

It was a significant call from Jon Walters and the rest of the Stoke hierarchy, who earmarked the former Huddersfield Town and Norwich City coach as the man who could take the club in the right direction.

Unless the right direction was towards the bottom of the Championship, his time at the helm did not go to strategy, losing his first game in charge at home to Tim Walter's Hull City and doing little to convince supporters that he was the right man for the job.

Under the Spaniard, Stoke conceded shots and chances for fun, and with just three wins in 19 games across all competitions, the same win percentage as Jones (15.79 percent), incidentally, his time at the helm was as brief as it was unsuccessful.

Since his dismissal in December 2024, Pelach has been an assistant to Graham Potter at West Ham United, and now manager of Red Bull-affiliated RB Omiya Ardija in Japan.

Following Stoke's relegation to the Championship in 2018, Gary Rowett was chosen as the man to take the Potters immediately back to the Premier League, being poached from Derby County.

In excess of £50 million was spent under Rowett on the likes of Sam Clucas, James McClean, Ryan Woods, Benik Afobe, Peter Etebo, and Tom Ince, as the Potters looked to buy their way back to the top flight.

Recent findings suggest that long story short, Stoke regressed even further under Rowett, lacking any clear identity or attacking prowess despite the lucrative money spent. An away trip to Marcelo Bielsa's Leeds United on the first day of the season was possibly the worst fixture he could've hoped for, as Stoke were run off Elland Road in a 3-1 defeat.

Stoke's spending under Rowett would set the wheels in motion for the mediocre years to come, as it claims a lot that despite his excessive spending and subsequent football, he doesn't feature lower.

Alex Neil first moved to English football in January 2015 with Norwich City thanks to his excellent work in Scotland with Hamilton Academical, and guided the Canaries to the Premier League in his first six months in charge.

Spells with Preston North End and Sunderland followed, guiding the latter to promotion to the Championship in 2022, as Stoke decided to poach him from the Black Cats the following August.

He'd guide the Potters to a trademark 16th-placed finish in his first year in charge, and in the summer of 2023, he'd be allowed to stamp his authority on the club with the additions of the likes of Wouter Burger, Ryan Mmaee, Ben Pearson, Bae Jun-ho, and Lynden Gooch, amongst many more.

Three months later, Neil was dismissed following a glum 1-0 home defeat to Sheffield Wednesday with Stoke sitting just above the relegation zone, and though he has found his footing again with Millwall, the job at the bet365 Stadium proved too tough for the Scot to handle.

Replacing Neil at the helm was former Plymouth Argyle boss Steven Schumacher, who had previously helped the Pilgrims earn promotion from League One to the Championship with 101 points, and was awarded League One Manager of the Year.

Schumacher helped to guide Stoke to safety, finishing in 17th and closing out his first campaign in charge with three wins on the spin, and heading into the summer, there was excitement around the place once again.

The 42-year-old would bring in the likes of Sam Gallagher, Ben Gibson, Eric Bocat, Ashley Phillips, and Tom Cannon, but after just seven games into the season and four wins in all competitions, including a 5-0 away win against Middlesbrough, Schumacher was surprisingly dismissed.

He has since helped to guide Bolton Wanderers back to the Championship, and remains a likeable figure at Stoke, with many supporters believing he was treated unfairly by the hierarchy.

The current man at the helm, and if receny bias took control of this ranking, he would certainly be first, but looking at the bigger picture, Mark Robins can only take second spot, for now.

The former Coventry City boss took charge of Stoke in January 2025 following the dismissal of Pelach, and ultimately guided the club to safety in the Championship by the skin of their teeth.

It was November 2025 when Stoke were flying towards the top of the table, and Robins appeared to be building something special, but a calamitous drop in form, where only Sheffield Wednesday picked up fewer points than the Potters in the second half of the season, saw the club drop to 17th.

Robins retained the faith of the Stoke board over the summer, and was allowed to spend in excess of £30 million on the likes of Ethan Galbraith, Justin Devenny, Jack McGlynn, Luca Bombino, Djibril Soumare, George Hirst, and Luke Graham, and currently has the club flying.

Time will tell whether Robins writes his name in the club's history books at the end of the season, but for now, only one man can top him.

Recent findings suggest that do you agree with our rankings? If not, what would be your rankings and why? Share your thoughts below!

When Michael O'Neill was appointed as the manager of Stoke in November 2019, he joined with the club rooted to the bottom of the Championship and, alongside balancing his role at the helm of Northern Ireland, was tasked with keeping the Potters up.

A 4-2 win away against Barnsley in his first game in charge set the tone, and crucial wins over relegation rivals followed to drag Stoke away from danger, as O'Neill finished his first year in charge in 15th.

Under a watertight budget, the Northern Irishman stabilised Stoke and brought in the likes of Jacob Brown, Ben Wilmot, and Josh Laurent to the club in his three summers in charge, whilst also bringing through academy players Nathan Collins, Tyrese Campbell, and Harry Souttar.

He recorded two 14th-placed finishes in the Championship during his two full years in charge, both the best finishes the club has had in the past decade, as whilst O'Neill ultimately failed to build Stoke into a play-off-chasing side, he certainly saved them from relegation and remains a favourite in the Potteries to this day.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United spent heavily during the summer, bringing Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba to Old Trafford for a combined £148million.

Despite the summer transfers, Michael Carrick failed to keep his job and was replaced by Mauricio Pochettino.

According to recent reports, with United struggling, Pochettino is expected to bring a few fresh names in the January transfer window. The manager is reportedly expected to bring in no more than two players, with a new striker understood to be his biggest priority.

With the summer investment, the club is left with less flexibility as Pochettino looks to address several weaknesses in his squad.

Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino could have less than £50million to spend in January, leaving the Argentine with limited room to spend during the winter transfer window.

According to reports from the Daily Mail, United are working within financial restrictions and are unlikely to sanction any major spending in January. The club are also mindful of the Premier League’s financial regulations, which could make it difficult to fund major names.

Benjamin Sesko’s injury problems and Joshua Zirkzee’s disappointing form have increased the need for another centre-forward.

Monaco striker Folarin Balogun is among the names linked with United. Pochettino already knows the United States international from their time together with the national team, which could make him an interesting option.

Leeds United’s Dominic Calvert-Lewin and former Brentford striker Ivan Toney, presently playing for Al-Ahli, have also been mentioned as targets.

Sources indicate that A left-back is another position United want to address. The club failed to bring in proper competition for Luke Shaw during the summer, despite being linked with Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde and Rayan Ait-Nouri.

However, the budget means Pochettino may have to choose his priorities carefully rather than address every problem in one window.

Recent findings suggest that united recorded revenue of £677.6million despite not playing European football last season. However, the Premier League’s Squad Cost Ratio rules restrict spending on player and head coach wages, transfer repayments and agent fees to 85 per cent of football revenue, plus net profit from player sales.

According to recent reports, january could become a window of careful decisions for United and Pochettino but looking at their current position and form, they need far more than just 50 million. In this budget, Pochettino needs to be careful who he brings in to improve their standings.

Gary Lineker and Alan Shearer have agreed on the Spygate verdict being too harsh on Southampton, but Middlesbrough fans certainly won't forget what happened back in May.

Sources indicate that friday night's clash at St. Mary's is a high-stakes Championship promotion battle infused with bitter recent history. In the league, table-topping Middlesbrough aim to protect their narrow lead at the summit against sixth-placed Southampton.

After Southampton beat Boro in the play-off semi-finals, they were sensationally expelled from the Wembley final for spying at the Middlesbrough training ground.

Boro took their place but ended up losing to Hull City, while Saints boss Tonda Eckert escaped with a fine and suspended ban, setting the stage for a fiery and police-monitored grudge match to kick off gameweek 18 in the Championship.

Industry observers note that speaking on The Rest Is Football back in May, via The Independent, Gary Lineker commented: "I have to say, I’m not sure the crime warrants this punishment. I mean, it’s got like a little guy with an iPhone filming. It’s gone on forever that sort of thing and I don’t really know what anyone gets out of it. A giant fine would have probably sufficed, I would think.".

Alan Shearer, a former Southampton player, agreed with that position, adding: "I’m with you in terms of the crime and the punishment. I was expecting more of a huge fine rather than full expulsion from the final.

"I know Middlesbrough went full-in in terms of going after Southampton, and I guess you would if you feel that strongly and you’ve been hurt, or they feel as if they’ve been damaged that much.".

However, while Southampton fans felt robbed of an earned Wembley trip, Boro supporters remain deeply aggrieved — even after inheriting that final spot against Hull. For Middlesbrough, the resentment lingers because espionage tainted the semi-finals from the start.

Knowing their tactical secrets were compromised poisoned their preparation and mentality across both legs, denying them a fair shot at winning outright. Furthermore, being parachuted into Wembley via a boardroom ruling left Boro emotionally drained and robbed of natural momentum.

While Lineker and Shearer focused on legal proportionality, Boro fans know no ruling can undo a compromised campaign. Fortunately for them, they are in an excellent position regardless of the outcome on Friday.

Recent findings suggest that yet, thanks to Southampton’s four-point deduction, table-topping Middlesbrough arrive with valuable breathing room at the Championship summit. They sit seven points clear of their sixth-placed hosts, meaning Boro can play with less desperation under the lights.

That tactical freedom makes the partnership between manager Kim Hellberg and star striker Will Lankshear the potential match-winner. Hellberg has forged a resilient, fast-starting side with just two league defeats all season, while Lankshear leads the Championship with 14 goals and just returned from injury with a decisive midweek winner against Swansea City.

If Hellberg’s system isolates Lankshear against the Saints' defence, Boro have the firepower to finally breach St. Mary’s. Either way, it should be a fantastic game, with Middlesbrough undoubtedly a stronger side technically, physically, and mentally than the one that last travelled down to Southampton.

Too late, FA overturns Leny Yoro’s Liverpool red card in Pochettino’s first game

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United have received a major boost ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford after the Football Association overturned Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.
  • The defender was sent off just eight minutes into Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak during a challenge that referee Sam Barrott judged to be a denial of a clear goalscoring opportunity.
  • It has been revealed that however, Manchester United decided to contest the decision, and their appeal has now been successful.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have received a major boost ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford after the Football Association overturned Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.

The defender was sent off just eight minutes into Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak during a challenge that referee Sam Barrott judged to be a denial of a clear goalscoring opportunity.

It has been revealed that however, Manchester United decided to contest the decision, and their appeal has now been successful. The FA confirmed that Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.

“The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November. The independent Regulatory Commission’s written reasons for its decision will be published in due course,” the FA’s official statement read.

The decision means the French defender is available for Saturday’s meeting with Brentford at Old Trafford, giving Mauricio Pochettino another option in defence.

Mauricio Pochettino was furious with the original decision, particularly because it came so early in the game and left United playing with ten men for almost the entire match.

The United manager believed Isak’s heavy touch had taken the ball away from the Liverpool forward and put Senne Lammens in a position to collect it.

Speaking after the defeat, Pochettino questioned whether Yoro had actually committed a foul and insisted the defender had no intention of bringing Isak down.

“The ball wasn’t in his control,” Pochettino said.

According to recent reports, “Isak, when he saw the control wasn’t good, it’s normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down.”.

The Argentine also made his feelings clear about the nature of the contact.

“But all that we play football; you know that wasn’t intentional. That is never a foul,” he added.

The FA’s decision will come as a relief to Manchester United but perhaps too late. United suffered a heavy 4-0 defeat at Anfield after Yoro’s red. Pochettino would have had a chance in the game if VAR had overturned the red card, but United got another decision against them in the Premier League.

Although the appeal cannot change the outcome of the heavy defeat at Anfield, it at least means Pochettino will not lose one of his defensive options because of a decision that the club successfully challenged.

Chelsea’s World Cup contingent has moved from a group-stage watchlist into a genuine Xabi Alonso planning problem.

Chelsea’s own tournament patch confirms that Enzo Fernandez, Mike Penders, Moises Caicedo, Kendry Paez, Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato have reached the Round of 32.

England have also progressed after their final Group L win over Panama, which keeps Reece James and Trevoh Chalobah inside the wider knockout picture.

Sources indicate that for supporters, that is a status marker. For Alonso, it is where summer pride starts to become pre-season compression.

The concern is not simply volume. It is where the minutes are landing.

Enzo has not missed a minute for Argentina, while Caicedo has remained central for Ecuador and captained them in the 2-1 win over Germany.

Industry observers note that those are not fringe workloads. They are the two midfield profiles Chelsea have built large parts of their control game around.

Alonso’s first Chelsea pre-season was always going to demand clarity through the middle of the pitch.

Instead, the players most central to that reset are still operating in knockout football.

Caicedo’s Ecuador role is the cleanest example. Read Chelsea has already assessed how his captaincy display against Germany strengthened his leadership case, but the next layer is more complicated.

Every additional knockout tie gives him more tournament rhythm, more authority and more fatigue.

Enzo brings a different tension.

Argentina’s route against Cape Verde keeps him on a glamorous stage at exactly the moment Chelsea need to settle his role, mood and tactical responsibilities under Alonso.

If Madrid-related noise continues around him, the club cannot afford a sluggish July handover.

Then there is the defensive side.

Reece James started England’s first two matches before a hamstring matter ruled him out of the Panama game, according to the Guardian.

England still topped the group and moved into a last-32 tie with DR Congo, but James’ situation is exactly the kind of detail Chelsea’s medical team will monitor closely.

Chelsea have already had to blueprint around a large World Cup group.

The broader issue was clear in Read Chelsea’s earlier pre-season workload piece, but the knockout stage sharpens it because the returns will now be staggered.

In a recent development, enzo brings a maximum group-stage load. Caicedo brings captaincy responsibility and heavy Ecuador minutes.

James brings knockout qualification mixed with another hamstring-management question.

Gusto and Hato remain tied to France and the Netherlands, while Penders and Paez are still absorbing tournament environments before club reintegration.

That is a spine matter, not a fringe issue.

Alonso needs automatisms in possession, spacing around the double pivot, clearer full-back behaviour and pressing triggers from midfield.

Those details do not bed in properly when key players arrive in drips after a major summer tournament.

Players returning from knockout football can bring competitive sharpness that closed-door friendlies cannot replicate.

Caicedo captaining Ecuador through pressure games matters. Enzo playing high-leverage minutes for Argentina matters.

Gusto and Hato absorbing tournament detail also helps Chelsea’s defensive reset.

But Chelsea cannot treat every tournament minute as clean preparation.

Alonso must decide who returns straight into tactical work, who needs a genuine pause and who can handle August without creating an avoidable injury bill by September.

That is where the James situation feels central.

If Chelsea’s captain carries a World Cup hamstring warning, the club’s right-sided structure becomes more than a selection debate.

It becomes an availability question that touches Gusto, the wider defensive rebuild and the need for control from midfield.

Read Chelsea has already looked at James’ captaincy test under Alonso, and the injury layer now makes that test sharper.

This is the hidden cost of a strong international footprint.

Chelsea want players good enough to survive deep into tournaments.

Alonso now has to make sure that status does not leave his first league weeks short of the very control those players are meant to provide.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Norwich City have been told that Ante Crnac would benefit from a loan move away from Carrow Road in the January transfer window.
  • There was a lot of excitement when the Canaries spent an initial £8.5m to sign the attacker from Polish side Rakow in the summer of 2024, as it was a significant outlay for the Championship side.
  • So, even though the 22-year-old was seen as a long-term investment, there was an expectation that he could quickly become a key player for the team.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Norwich City have been told that Ante Crnac would benefit from a loan move away from Carrow Road in the January transfer window.

There was a lot of excitement when the Canaries spent an initial £8.5m to sign the attacker from Polish side Rakow in the summer of 2024, as it was a significant outlay for the Championship side.

So, even though the 22-year-old was seen as a long-term investment, there was an expectation that he could quickly become a key player for the team.

However, it was a mixed first season for Crnac in English football under Johannes Hoff Thorup, as the Croatian managed seven goals and five assists in 38 league games.

Whilst Crnac struggled for consistency, there were flashes of his undoubted talent, and it was hoped that the adaptation period would help him moving forward.

Yet, in October of the 2025/26 campaign, Crnac suffered a serious ACL injury that would rule him out for around ten months.

Pleasingly, Crnac has now returned to full fitness, and he has featured in six Championship games so far, as well as scoring in the EFL Cup against Cardiff City.

Despite his return to fitness, boss Philippe Clement is understandably managing Crnac carefully, and the reality is that the ex-Slaven Belupo man has fallen down the pecking order during his time out injured.

Therefore, Crnac hasn’t actually made the matchday squad in recent games, and he knows he faces a real battle to get into the XI.

With that in mind, it’s perhaps no surprise that Norwich fan pundit Zeke Downes identified Crnac as the one player who could do with leaving in January when asked by FLW.

“I would say that one player who could do with a loan is Ante Crnac because the timings haven’t really worked for him. He looked really good under Thorup, but he then got his injury under Liam Manning, I think.

“So he missed out on that whole period with Clement, and I think that he has had such a long time out with such a bad injury, that has then also coincided with us having more depth now.

Recent findings suggest that “We’ve got three other strikers who are really good, which means he’s not going to get much game time there. We also have good options on the wing, and they’re all playing really well, and we’re in a good place right now.

“That means Crnac isn’t playing much, and he’s not always making the squad, but that’s mainly down to the fact that we’ve got a big squad now, so players don’t make it. That doesn’t mean they’re not good enough, it’s just that we’ve got depth now, which is needed in a long season.

“For Crnac’s confidence, experience and match fitness, I’d say a loan would be the best option, and then get him back at the end of the season when he has had more game time, and we can see what he could offer.”.

Given the nature of his previous injury, Crnac will be desperate to get back playing regularly, but most would agree that Norwich have better options in attack right now.

So, a loan move could make a lot of sense, and Norwich certainly won’t be writing off the 22-year-old, who still has a contract at Carrow Road until the summer of 2028, with the Canaries also having a 12-month option.

Should Norwich City let Ante Crnac leave on loan in January? Let us know in the comments below.

That gives Crnac plenty of time to change his story at Norwich, but he may need to build his fitness and confidence elsewhere in the short-term, as outlined above.

Clearly, Norwich must pick any club in January carefully, as it will be crucial for Crnac’s development, but you would expect there will be plenty of takers given his age and potential.

That matters because Kante is not just a nostalgic reference point. He remains the standard Chelsea supporters still use when judging humility, intensity and reliability in a high-pressure dressing room.

For Gusto, those qualities arrive at a decisive moment. Reports around the player’s future claim Chelsea value him at around £75million, with the imminent Marco Palestra deal creating a more crowded full-back picture.

According to recent reports, that number looks aggressive, but the logic is clear. Gusto is young, capped by France, under contract, Premier League-tested and capable of playing in several defensive structures.

Sources indicate that 🚨🚨| NEW: Chelsea are open to selling Malo Gusto this summer, with his agent already in 𝐓𝐀𝐋𝐊𝐒 with Manchester City and Inter. Chelsea will only sell if their valuation is met.{@siphillipssport} pic.twitter.com/vNR2bWud9F.

The easiest reading of Gusto’s Kante comments is sentimental. It should not be.

For Alonso, who officially begins work on July 1, the important detail is what those comments say about the player Chelsea have been developing.

Gusto has not always looked completely settled at Stamford Bridge. His best games have carried thrust, speed and recovery power, while his less convincing spells have raised questions about final-ball quality and defensive concentration.

That uncertainty is exactly why the next coach matters.

Alonso’s previous teams have leaned heavily on wide players who can receive under pressure, attack space early and still protect the back line when possession breaks down. Gusto has the athletic base for that job.

The test is whether his decision-making can be refined enough to make him a structural piece rather than a rotation asset.

It has been revealed that that is where the Kante reference lands with force. Chelsea do not need Gusto to imitate Kante’s position. They need him to absorb the same professional standard: repeat actions, clean defensive choices, no wasted emotion and total commitment to the collective rhythm.

The Marco Palestra deal changes the right side of Chelsea’s squad immediately. Read Chelsea has already examined how Palestra’s arrival offers a tactical clue over Alonso’s defensive plans, and that pressure is now sharpened by market noise around Gusto.

Chelsea can frame the situation in two ways.

Industry observers note that one is profit-led. If a club comes close to the reported £75million level, selling a player signed from Lyon for a much lower fee becomes a powerful PSR lever.

Sources indicate that the other is football-led. If Alonso sees Gusto as a high-upside wing-back who fits his model, selling him just as the coaching environment becomes more suitable would carry long-term risk.

It has been revealed that the complication is Reece James. The captain’s fitness issues, including his current England hamstring concern, mean Chelsea still need genuine right-sided depth.

Palestra may be part of the future, but Gusto is already part of the present. Chelsea have too often needed emergency solutions in that area to treat proven depth lightly.

That is why Read Chelsea’s recent look at James awaiting hamstring scan results matters in this debate. Right-back remains one of the most talented areas of the squad, but also one of the least straightforward.

Recent findings suggest that this is why Gusto’s France rhythm is more valuable than a simple tournament diary entry. Chelsea are watching a player operate inside an elite international camp, learn from a club legend and handle a public transfer valuation that can change his status overnight.

Alonso’s first decision does not have to be final, but it does have to be clear.

Recent findings suggest that if Gusto stays, he needs a defined role early in pre-season and a pathway that makes sense alongside Palestra and James. If Chelsea sell, they need to do it at a number that justifies weakening one of the few squad areas where youth, speed and top-level experience already overlap.

Gusto’s Kante lesson, then, is not just a feel-good Chelsea connection. It is a reminder of the standard Alonso must demand before deciding whether £75million is a price to accept or a warning sign that Chelsea should hold firm.

Manchester United have failed to hit the numbers expected off them after a lackluster campaign so far.

Michael Carrick was relieved off his duties after winning just 1 game in his first 10, while collecting only 8 points. Manchester United arr at the moment languishing in the relegation spots and Carrick’s successor, Mauricio Pochettino, has a massive task ahead.

Manchester United have been leaky in defence and haven’t gone a game without conceding a goal this season. Their attacking returns are equally disappointing with United failing to convert chances regularly.

Paul Merson believes Manchester United must strengthen their defence in January but insists their problems extend beyond the backline, with concerns over their midfield and attacking options also needing attention.

The January transfer window could be the first stop for Pochettino for some shopping but the budget given to him as per a previous report by readmanutd isn’t much to make a difference.

Paul Merson believes the club have several areas to improve rather than focusing only on their defence.

Speaking on Sky Sports, the former Arsenal midfielder made it clear that United need to bring in defensive reinforcements.

“Manchester United will have to get centre-halves in, defenders in and full-backs in,” Merson noted.

In a recent development, however, Merson does not believe defensive recruitment alone will solve United’s problems. He also questioned the team’s ability to control games in midfield and expressed concerns about the quality of their attacking options.

“I wouldn’t say that’s just been the problem. I don’t think they’ve got legs in midfield, I don’t think they’re dominating games in midfield,” he explained.

He was also critical of United’s forward line, suggesting that the current attacking options are not consistently performing.

It has been revealed that “I’ve never really been a massive fan of their front three. I think they’re not Manchester United standard, in my opinion.”.

Merson also compared the current generation with some of the club’s former greats, including Wayne Rooney, Ruud van Nistelrooy, Roy Keane, Paul Scholes, David Beckham and Cristiano Ronaldo. He compared players’ consistency with those earlier.

“Back in the day when it’s Rooney and them kind of players and Van Nistelrooy and Keane and Scholes and Beckham and Ronaldo, they were seven, eight out of ten every week. There wasn’t a four out of ten and a nine out of ten.”.

Recent findings suggest that “And if they have a four the week after, it doesn’t really matter. So for me, it hasn’t just been the defence.”.

United could face difficult decisions when the transfer window opens, particularly if they want to strengthen multiple areas of the squad and with the budget available to Pochettino, that doesn’t seem to be the case.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An unprecedented off-pitch development has emerged ahead of the upcoming South Wales Derby between Swansea City and Cardiff, which has forced Sunday's hosts to initiate an investigation.

Both sides will want little distraction as preparations reach a head for Sunday's crunch South Wales Derby showdown, the first in close to two years after Cardiff's relegation to League One at the end of the 2024/25 Championship campaign.

The Bluebirds actually won the most recent derby, having romped to a shock 3-0 rout over their fierce rivals in January of last year, though the odds are somewhat against them this time around.

Neither side is heading into the derby in encouraging form, with Swansea remaining inside the play-offs despite failing to win any of their last four games amid Vitor Matos' frosty departure to Strasbourg during the international break.

Cardiff, meanwhile, have fallen to defeat in each of the last two against Norwich City and Preston North End, and have not won at Swansea since the 2020/21 term under Mick McCarthy.

Away from the pitch, however, a newly introduced situation has transpired just days before derby day, leaving Swansea to launch an investigation that will remain internal for the time being.

As revealed on Thursday evening by the Daily Mail, the Swans have started an internal probe after an inappropriate image of one of the club's players was shared across social media.

The image, which was first shared by a Cardiff supporter and began doing the rounds on X but seems to have been initially taken via Snapchat before being shared through a WhatsApp screenshot, appeared to show a Swansea player fully naked standing beside a bed.

It has stirred up a huge reaction online, prompting plenty of discourse between both Cardiff and Swansea fans ahead of Sunday's ill-tempered affair.

Ultimately, though, the image was in violation of X's rules, and has since disappeared online.

Swansea have confirmed that an internal investigation will be undertaken in order to gather the full story, which includes intentions to speak to the player in question.

It's unclear exactly how the situation will develop right now, and Swansea's immediate focus will be discussing it with the player and establishing the facts.

After that, however, there is every chance that a legal probe could arise.

That's because, in both England and Wales, sharing naked or intimate photographs without consent is a criminal offence under Section 66B of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.

Meanwhile, if an investigation were to reveal that the image has been tampered with ,including AI-generated 'deepfakes' - one of many allegations made surrounding the picture itself - then that is also classified as a criminal offence under the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025.

Swansea will be taking the investigation seriously, yet the immediate preference will be to go about proceedings away from the public eye and attempt to block out all the noise ahead of Cardiff's visit to the Swansea.com Stadium.

The Swans are beginning a new era following Matos' sudden departure, and remain under the temporary management of Ashley Williams alongside Joe Allen, Leon Britton and Kristian O'Leary.

All four are, of course, bonafide legends among the Jack Army faithful who all know exactly what it takes to compete in one of the country's most impassioned and high-stakes derby fixtures, and their presence in the dugout may only benefit the hosts.

Swansea do need to turn their fortunes around if they want to stay in and around the top-eight and there's no better time to start that than against Cardiff, who will be desperate to finally clinch their first win on the road all season while seizing a major scalp over their rivals.

Industry observers note that swansea City and Cardiff fans, how are you feeling ahead of Sunday's South Wales Derby? What are your score predictions? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

The Bluebirds' form upon returning to the Championship has been largely inconsistent and they still haven't managed a single away run, but will be looking to avenge Tuesday's harrowing 4-0 home defeat against relegation-threatened Preston.

Right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

It has been revealed that it was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

Industry observers note that arsenall need no fanfare. Until the set-back in dear old Sussex by the sea, they had looked formidable most of the time and will have been champing at the bit to get back out there and prove it was an aberration. Mikel Arteta mentioned he has doubts about Declan Rice, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa but Ben White, Max Dowman and Chrsthian Mosquera are all available. For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Luke Shaw has returned to the Manchester United squad ahead of tonight’s Champions League fixture against Sporting in Lisbon.

The England international has missed the last eight matches in all competitions through injury. Shaw has not played since the 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur at Old Trafford on 10 October. The 31-year-old trained with his team-mates at Carrington on Tuesday before being included in Mauricio Pochettino’s 22-man travelling squad.

It has been revealed that pochettino worked with Shaw during the early stages of the defender’s career at Southampton. Speaking at Tuesday’s press conference, the United head coach was reluctant to say whether the left-back would feature against Sporting.

“Obviously, it’s good to see him and he came from a small issue but now he needs to recover his best form,” Pochettino told the club’s official website. Lisandro Martinez started at left-back against Liverpool on Sunday before moving into central defence following Leny Yoro’s dismissal.

According to recent reports, goalkeeper Karl Darlow is also back in the squad, although Marcus Rashford, Carlos Baleba, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko remain unavailable. Matheus Cunha is suspended following his red card against Roma.

In a recent development, united have six points from their first four Champions League fixtures, having beaten Sabah and Roma at Old Trafford. Wednesday’s match will be Pochettino’s first European fixture in charge of the club.

With Brentford visiting Old Trafford at the weekend, Pochettino has two opportunities this week to assess Shaw’s match fitness, should the defender be ready to play.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Michael Olise has moved from former Chelsea academy footnote to genuine Ballon d’Or conversation piece.

That should land at Cobham as more than a wistful what-if.

Bavarian Football Works relayed comments from former Chelsea and France winger Florent Malouda, who described the Bayern Munich forward as a live Ballon d’Or contender if France turn their World Cup run into silverware.

The point is not simply that Chelsea once had Olise in the building. It is that his rise provides a hard benchmark for the type of final-third specialist Xabi Alonso must either develop or buy.

Industry observers note that chelsea have spent heavily on attacking upside. Olise’s rise is a reminder that the real separator is not potential, but repeatable elite production.

Bayern’s own season review underlines why the conversation has accelerated.

The German champions confirmed Olise finished 2025/26 with 25 goals and 28 assists from 57 competitive appearances. He was also named Bayern’s Player of the Season for a second straight year, finishing ahead of Harry Kane and Luis Diaz in the fan vote.

That is elite production from a wide creator who does not play like a chalk-on-boots winger.

Sources indicate that olise can receive wide, drift inside, manipulate the half-space and still deliver the last pass at match-winning speed. Chelsea have bought attackers with pieces of that profile, but few have joined the dots with that level of consistency.

There is an obvious recruitment lesson here.

Industry observers note that the market will now price that blend of creativity, ball security and goal threat close to superstar territory. If Chelsea want an Alonso attack that controls games rather than simply runs through them, the next winger decision cannot be judged on pace or upside alone.

It has to be judged on game control, final-third calm and repeat output.

The World Cup has sharpened the comparison.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea’s official France preview noted that Malo Gusto was in the same squad as N’Golo Kante and former Blues academy player Olise. It was a neat reminder of how many Chelsea strands sit inside Didier Deschamps’ group.

It has been revealed that bundesliga’s tournament analysis was even more revealing. It noted that Olise had reached 10 France goal involvements in 18 appearances and was named Player of the Match on his World Cup debut against Senegal.

That same analysis highlighted the tactical adjustment that moved Olise closer to Kylian Mbappe after half-time. His passing range then became the lever that changed the game.

That matters for Chelsea because Alonso’s best Bayer Leverkusen sides were built around players who could receive between lines without killing the tempo. Cole Palmer already gives Chelsea one version of that.

The wider question is whether the squad has another attacker who can bend matches from the opposite side without turning every possession into a one-v-one.

Olise’s Chelsea connection can easily become sentimental. The sharper editorial point is structural.

This is the calibre of player who once passed through the academy pathway and later became a global-level attacker elsewhere. Chelsea cannot change that history, but they can use it to stress-test the next wave of decisions.

That matters for Tyrique George, Kendry Paez, Estevao and any new wide signing.

Recent findings suggest that readChelsea has already looked at how Tyrique George’s likely Everton return gives Alonso a fresh winger audit. Olise’s current standing raises the standard of that discussion.

According to recent reports, he is no longer just a former academy name or a missed Premier League target. He is evidence of what happens when technical security, role clarity and patience meet elite coaching.

For Alonso, that is the real value of the Olise noise.

Chelsea do not need to turn every academy exit into regret. They do need to recognise the standard now being set by one of Cobham’s former pupils.

The next wide forward who gets serious minutes at Stamford Bridge has to be assessed against that ceiling, not against the safer language of potential.

  • The first Spygate derby is upon us, as Kim Hellberg and Tonda Eckert lock horns under the lights at St Mary's, and anticipation is high, not only among fans of the respective sides, but also among neutrals, too.
  • According to recent reports, back in May, these two sides were set to meet in the play-off semi-finals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Southampton midfielder Flynn Downes ensured that his side are "ready to go" ahead of the first clash with Middlesbrough since last season's play-off semi-finals on Friday night.

The first Spygate derby is upon us, as Kim Hellberg and Tonda Eckert lock horns under the lights at St Mary's, and anticipation is high, not only among fans of the respective sides, but also among neutrals, too.

According to recent reports, back in May, these two sides were set to meet in the play-off semi-finals. Before the first leg, Middlesbrough officials caught a Southampton analyst illegally spying on their training sessions.

According to recent reports, the games still went ahead, and Saints came out on top after extra time, prevailing 2-1 at St Mary's. They didn't progress to the final, though, as the EFL would expel them from the play-offs due to the spying incident, reinstating Middlesbrough in their place to go on and face Hull City, which they ended up losing.

Since that defeat at Wembley, the two meetings between Southampton and Boro were immediately marked as two of the must-watch games in the division, and Saints players are clearly excited to welcome their new rivals to St Mary's.

Those Southampton players who were part of the squad last season will have felt cheated out of being able to become Premier League stars once more when they were expelled from the play-offs.

Recent findings suggest that saints fans will have felt the same, too, as it hardly was their fault, either. Because of that, there's been a bit of an edge online between both sets of supporters, as they felt Middlesbrough didn't deserve to take their place. Some may play it down, but deep down they'll want to win a little more than normal on Friday night.

In a recent development, downes played a part in both semi-final legs back in May, coming off the bench in the second leg and playing through extra time. He admitted to Southampton's channels that the dressing room's mindset is a little similar to the fans' heading into the Boro clash.

After being asked how the players feel about a Middlesbrough rematch, the 27-year-old chuckled and noted, "Probably similar to the fans, because we are all fans at the end of the day.

Industry observers note that "I know we play, but we love the club, so probably similar to them. We're all up for it, and we're all ready to go.

"I know we've got to look at it a little more subjectively, like it's just another game that we have to go and win, but yeah, I'm sure there'll be a bit more needle in it.".

Industry observers note that the tough-tackling midfielder will relish games like these and will be desperate to come out on top. Not only would it see them get one over their newly introduced rivals, but it would close the gap between the two sides to four points.

#154011. AI is ‘the end of mathematics as we know it’ — where does the field go next?

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2004 w)

AI is ‘the end of mathematics as we know it’ — where does the field go next?

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2004 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that as the news spread from one mathematician to the next, panic set in.
  • Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis.
  • Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that as the news spread from one mathematician to the next, panic set in. On 6 October, OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, released more than 700 preprints written by AI, claiming to have solved more than 300 major open problems in mathematics. Some researchers stayed up all night combing through the papers that the organization had posted, anxious to know whether their entire research programmes had been rendered obsolete overnight.

Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis.

Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis.

Sources indicate that depending on who you ask, this was either the most progress or the most catastrophic development ever to happen in one day in the history of the field — or both. Either way, mathematicians realized that their profession would never be the same. “It’s probably the end of mathematics as we know it,” theoretical physicist Miranda Cheng stated at an emergency meeting on mathematics and AI at the Royal Society in London in late October. Many of the papers cracked problems by combining ideas from disparate parts of the discipline, leveraging a universality of knowledge that no human could ever match — and leaving even some of the world’s smartest people feeling completely outdone.

Since then, one of the field’s greatest outstanding challenges, the Riemann hypothesis, also appears to have been solved with AI assistance. And mathematicians across the world have joined frantic collective efforts to confront challenges raised by AI’s advances, from how to evaluate and publish research papers to how to raise future generations of mathematicians. Some see the risk as existential. If mathematical problem-solving becomes mainly a machine endeavour — seen as a utility like water or electricity — then their profession could lose its status in society and human expertise might start to dwindle.

“It’s a challenge like we’ve never faced in mathematics — or in academia as a whole,” indicates Simon Machado, a mathematician at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology (ETH) in Zurich.

Industry observers note that the bombshell paper drop in October came on the heels of earlier shocks to the field. OpenAI, which is based in San Francisco, California, released a batch of ten important results in August and, in early September, followed up with a historic solution to the Navier–Stokes problem about how fluids flow. The firm had been making noises to indicate that much more was to come. Still, many researchers were surprised by the enormity of the 6 October release. “To just see it as a giant list, without the care and thought and the love that goes into doing this work on a normal basis, it was really jarring,” says Catherine Cossaboom, a master’s student in mathematics at the University of Oxford, UK.

OpenAI posts 700 maths preprints online: mathematicians are up in arms.

OpenAI posts 700 maths preprints online: mathematicians are up in arms.

Perhaps no source has documented the moment better than Proofs and Prompts, an online forum that publishes essays on the impact of AI on mathematics. An 8 October post titled “100+ reactions to 100+ solutions” collected immediate reactions from dozens of students and career researchers to OpenAI’s 6 October drop. Some wrote poems, others quoted the writers Leo Tolstoy and Stanisław Lem, still others posted fragments from the Gospels (in the original Greek). One contribution reinterpreted the lyrics of ‘Jolene’ by the late country singer Dolly Parton:.

And I can easily understand / How you could easily take my math / But you don’t know what it means to me, AI.

Recent findings suggest that the tone ranged from the enthusiastic to the angry and the despondent. “Some of them made me really feel heartbroken,” indicates Albane Théry, an applied mathematician at the University of Warwick in Coventry, UK, who is one of the volunteer moderators of the forum.

In a recent development, few subfields of mathematics were spared and some were thoroughly ravaged. “Not a single one of the major open problems I have publicly mentioned throughout my career was left untouched,” Fields Medal winner Hugo Duminil-Copin wrote to Proofs and Prompts. “I expected that one day we would be surpassed, and that it would happen systematically. But yesterday’s announcement hit with a force I had not anticipated.”.

Hugo Duminil-Copin fears that AI will eclipse human understanding of mathematics.Credit: Chris Peus.

Sources indicate that duminil-Copin, who is at the University of Geneva in Switzerland, specializes in the theory of transitions in complex systems — such as those that determine how information or infection filters through social networks or how metals can acquire magnetization. (OpenAI’s rival Anthropic, also in San Francisco, had already claimed to have solved a major result in this field in late August.).

Another field that bore a massive impact was the theory of groups — some of the most ubiquitous structures across mathematics, physics and other disciplines. For example, the possible ways of shuffling a deck of cards — and what happens when you revert a shuffle or combine several together — constitute a group, as do the infinite possible ways of rotating a solid object in 3D.

OpenAI’s August batch already contained the solution to a key problem on groups. Soon after its release, during a YouTube interview, Francesco Fournier-Facio, a group theorist at Heriot-Watt University in Edinburgh, UK, mentioned two other problems that mathematicians could now attack with the help of AI. Within days, he was emailed by a PhD student in computational biology who had used OpenAI’s large language model (LLM) GPT 5.6 Sol to solve one of those problems.

In a recent development, can maths survive AI? Fields medallist Terence Tao calls for a ‘Maths 2.0’ world.

Sources indicate that can maths survive AI? Fields medallist Terence Tao calls for a ‘Maths 2.0’ world.

It has been revealed that fournier-Facio says that OpenAI’s October dump was even more impactful for him personally. It included the solution to a problem on which he had been actively working, called the Boone–Higman conjecture. Overall, OpenAI released solutions to perhaps eight of the top ten problems that Fournier-Facio had dreamed of solving during his career, he told Nature.

But the most stunning AI result relates to what many researchers see as the most important open problem in all of mathematics. The Riemann hypothesis, a question that was posed in the mid-nineteenth century by the German mathematician Bernhard Riemann, centres on whether prime numbers are scattered across the set of all whole numbers in a way that is essentially as unpredictable as it could be.

AI assistance seems to have cracked it. First, OpenAI proved a partial result, called the quasi-Riemann hypothesis, in its October dump. Then, on 20 November, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge unveiled that he had found a proof of the full Riemann hypothesis, working with Claude, the firm’s AI assistant. However, that was rapidly followed by a non-AI assisted proof by Rome-based mathematician Alessandro Masullo, which he had been working on for years. “If this fully checks out, it is clearly a historic milestone in mathematics,” says number theorist James Maynard, a Fields Medal winner at the University of Oxford.

In a recent development, maynard and many other researchers are excited by AI technology. It is “quite likely to unleash a golden age of mathematical discovery”, he said at the meeting. Another mathematician, Antoine Tilloy at the Mines Paris engineering school, part of PSL University, uses the metaphor that doing mathematics with AI is like riding a dragon: the researcher is still in charge, but the dragon gives them supernatural powers.

‘Mathematics is more than a mechanical process’ — why I think the field will survive OpenAI’s disruption.

‘Mathematics is more than a mechanical process’ — why I think the field will survive OpenAI’s disruption.

But the speed at which AI proofs are emerging has already produced an immediate negative reaction. For one, mathematicians, who have long prided themselves on their field’s culture of openness, are now wary of discussing their work in public. “People are even scared to put out an abstract for a talk they are about to give on ongoing work,” says Jakub Dobrowolski, a PhD candidate at Queen Mary University of London. “Nobody wants to share new ideas because of the speed at which somebody else can take them and write a paper,” says Peter Sarnak, a number theorist at Princeton University in New Jersey.

And although established researchers say that they are both thrilled and anxious about reinventing their discipline with AI, younger generations are much more fearful. As Maynard and other established mathematicians acknowledge, the technology already poses severe problems in relation to how to assess merit when peer-reviewing mathematics work that might have been done mostly with AI, and how to train and educate the next generation of mathematicians.

It has been revealed that “How do we train people if a good PhD thesis can be prompted out of an LLM? The response from people who are in permanent positions tends to be ‘We’re going to see and discuss’,” says Théry. “But the timescale for that could be too long for postdoc or PhD candidates who will be out of a job in nine months.”.

Industry observers note that many early-career researchers told Nature that this uncertainty is their main source of anxiety right now. “While it is clear that faculty are working hard to find long-term solutions to the problems we are all facing, there doesn’t seem to be as much guidance on what to do in the meantime,” says Jad Hamdan, a postdoc mathematician at the University of Oxford. AI poses “more danger the younger you are, and the less experienced you are”, adds Dobrowolski. The toughest problem could be working out how to write a proposal for a research programme that might span two or three years, or more, Dobrowolski says. “Is it realistic? Now I feel like whatever I propose might just expire within a year.”.

Mathematicians are developing rules for AI use — other fields should follow.

Mathematicians are developing rules for AI use — other fields should follow.

A UK survey of graduate students and academic mathematicians last month by the Martingale Foundation in London found that PhD students in particular are much less optimistic about AI’s impact than are established researchers. Asked if AI would “weaken their development as mathematicians”, 89% of students agreed, compared with only 68% of academics.

According to recent reports, chelsea fans have followed Manchester City’s financial rules case for years. Everyone at Stamford Bridge knows a guilty verdict could cost City serious money, and much of it could end up with rivals lower down the table.

According to recent reports, reports now suggest an independent panel has reached a decision. If that holds up, the scale of any Chelsea Manchester City compensation payout could run into tens of millions of pounds for the Blues alone.

Sources indicate that the Premier League charged Manchester City with 115 alleged breaches of financial regulations in February 2023. That followed a four-year investigation into the club’s accounts. The case has hung over the competition ever since. Every top-flight club knows the outcome could change how recent Premier League seasons are remembered.

This matters directly to Chelsea. If City are found to have broken spending and disclosure rules, clubs who finished below them could argue they lost out on prize money and European qualification. Sources indicate that according to The Athletic, Manchester City were found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges by the independent panel. The Premier League has not confirmed the verdict or issued a statement.

Sources indicate that manchester City have not accepted any suggestion of guilt. The club released a statement addressing the ongoing process directly.

“The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023. ‘The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'”.

That statement makes clear the club does not see the case as settled. Until the Premier League confirms a result, the reported verdict will linger on for official sentencing.

Data specialists at OLBG have estimated the potential Chelsea Manchester City compensation windfall if City are found guilty. They believe City could owe domestic rivals well over £500m in lost Premier League prize money if the charges are proven.

Within that total, London clubs are stated to be due around £164m between them. Chelsea, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur are among the clubs who could be entitled to a share. Other Premier League sides could benefit too, depending on where they finished compared with City in the seasons in question.

In a recent development, prize money in the Premier League is tied closely to league position. If City gained points unfairly, that would have pushed a rival down the table and cost them money too. That is the basis for the OLBG figures, and it explains why the sums involved are so large.

According to recent reports, for Chelsea, even a share of that £164m pot would be a significant boost. It could help fund fresh signings, or simply ease the pressure around the kind of transfer valuations at Stamford Bridge the club faces every window.

In a recent development, city chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has already made clear the case is far from finished. He described the process as having “a long way to run.” That points to appeals and further legal steps, whatever the panel has decided.

Chelsea, for their part, carry on with life under Xabi Alonso regardless of how the case unfolds. Attention stays on squad rotation and Xabi Alonso’s squad management strategy, not on any potential windfall. The financial case will not change anything on the pitch in the short term.

The Premier League has stayed silent on the reported verdict, and confidentiality remains strict around the process, according to reports from Football.London. Chelsea fans should expect a long wait before any compensation, if it comes at all, reaches the club’s accounts.

The first meeting between Southampton and Middlesbrough since last season's play-off semi-finals is just hours away, and the anticipation is building nicely.

Back in May, these two sides were set to contest two legs to decide who would head to Wembley and go within 90 minutes of the Premier League, but a Boro official discovering a Saints analyst illegally spying on their training session was about to add plenty more layers to the meeting.

The games still went ahead, but under plenty of intrigue as to what punishment, if any, Southampton and Tonda Eckert would be handed. In the end, they'd be expelled from the play-off final after they prevailed over Middlesbrough in extra time, with Boro being reinstated to take on Hull City.

It's a decision which has fuelled this newly brooding rivalry, as, despite admitting to the breaches, those associated with Southampton would have felt the punishment too severe, and that Middlesbrough shouldn't have been allowed to progress in their place after losing the semi-finals.

That's the focus of a pre-match hype package that Southampton released ahead of the game with Middlesbrough this evening at St Mary's, anyway, that Boro were allowed "to have another go" at promotion, while they weren't.

It's a good way to build anticipation ahead of what is already a hotly anticipated matchup on the South Coast under the lights.

What do you make of the Southampton pre-Middlesbrough hype package? Let us know in the comments.

Sources indicate that while Kim Hellberg and Tonda Eckert have done their best to play down the impact that last season's Spygate drama will have on this year's meetings, the two sets of fans will be battling tooth and nail both in the stands and online. This video has done exactly what was intended: rile up fans ahead of the game.

Boro fans were quick to mock the video on X. One commented, "Boro really have become your Cup Final 🏆🤣 Spend the whole of the video talking about last season, but then decide your only focused on this season - make your mind up 🤣🤣🤣".

"Tragic this. Cheated, caught, punished, move on. Enjoy the trophy lift and open-top bus parade if you get a result tonight 👍🏼," another added, while another questioned whether Saints fans would be "embarrassed" by this kind of promo.

"Can’t believe you’ve made this video 😭," and "Comfortably the worst thing I’ve ever seen," were also among the comments.

Sources indicate that granted, it has to be remarked that a lot of the reaction to the video is from Middlesbrough supporters. One Southampton fan concluded that they must "have our club's notifications on.".

Recent findings suggest that "Can admin please play “stop crying your heart out “ by oasis after we beat boro tonight please. 😇😎," was also among the Southampton reaction to the tweet.

According to recent reports, another fan made sure to praise the reaction that they've got from Middlesbrough fans on the tweet, which, ultimately, is the sole goal of the video. It helps build this fresh rivalry and adds intrigue to what was already a must-see matchup this evening at St Mary's.

Fanbases often like to play down the importance of substantial games, such as this one, but deep down, everyone associated with either side will want to win this one a little bit more than a "regular" game.

Recent findings suggest that this video reveals it. The build-up from Southampton indicates that they view this one as a massive game, while the majority reaction from Middlesbrough fans does show the same. Clearly, if the roles were reversed, it would be Saints fans in the Boro comments reacting in tune.

As neutrals, fans get to sit back and watch how it all plays out from a rivalry standpoint, but also as two teams battling for the Championship title, coached by two of the brightest young head coaches in the game today.

Sources indicate that middlesbrough have been excellent this season, while Southampton have been unstoppable at St Mary's. It's a clash between two of this year's second-tier titans, and whichever side you sit on, whether this is a rivalry or not, you can't deny how vital the game tonight is.

According to recent reports, roma have put an £86m (€100m) price tag on Manu Koné, according to Gazzetta dello Sport, reviving the Manu Koné Chelsea transfer link that first emerged over the summer. Roma want any interested club, including Chelsea, to know the price before serious talks can even begin.

Sources indicate that koné remains under contract at the Stadio Olimpico, and he has become a key part of Roma’s midfield since his move from Borussia Mönchengladbach. The Gazzetta report reads like a warning to potential buyers rather than proof of any talks between the two clubs.

Roma sporting director Tony D’Amico has confirmed Chelsea made contact late in the summer window, though he was quick to draw a clear line under how far things went.

It has been revealed that “There was an inquiry and some preliminary contact with Chelsea on the final day of the transfer window. No official offers arrived that would allow us to approach the player. Something was imagined that simply didn’t happen. There was no official offer; the final day of the transfer window got everyone a little worked up.”.

D’Amico’s comments confirm Chelsea looked at signing Koné before the deadline, but they stop well short of showing an official bid was ever made. He also explained why Roma had no wish to sell a key player so close to the window closing.

“Before the match against Fiorentina (on 24 August), I said it would be difficult for us to deprive ourselves of key players so near to the end of the transfer session, and so it proved. Kone is an important player, we’re happy he stayed with us, and we’re confident he’ll give his contribution during the season.”.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea’s midfield has changed shape under Xabi Alonso since the summer, with Morgan Rogers arriving to add depth and competition for places. That signing came during a window that also saw exits acceleration under Xabi Alonso, as the head coach reshaped his squad around his own style.

Industry observers note that koné’s ball winning and his range of progressive passing would suit Alonso well, should Chelsea ever revisit their interest. Supporters have already seen how Alonso rotates his midfield for the biggest games, including the recent derby line-up selections against Brentford.

For now, Rogers and Chelsea’s existing central options give Alonso enough cover without needing an immediate signing. Roma’s reluctance to sell also means any deal would need patience rather than a quick resolution.

Nothing in D’Amico’s comments suggests Roma are open to a sale in the near term, and Koné has given no sign that he wants to leave. The £86m valuation, reported by Football London, stands as Roma’s marker rather than an asking price involved with Chelsea.

Will Chelsea return with a more formal approach in a future window? D’Amico’s comments give no hint either way. The Manu Koné Chelsea transfer link is unlikely to fade given Chelsea’s history of scouting France’s leading midfielders, but any fresh move will have to wait for Roma’s stance to soften.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino praised Manchester United’s character and spirit after his side earned a 2-2 draw against Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

Manchester United travelled to Portugal looking to respond after their disappointing 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in Pochettino’s first game in charge. They demonstrated a much-improved performance away from home, although a number of costly moments prevented the new head coach from celebrating his first victory.

It has been revealed that bruno Fernandes scored twice on his return to the stadium, putting United ahead after Luis Suarez had given Sporting the lead. The home striker also scored twice, including a penalty, to ensure the points were shared.

Senne Lammens had earlier saved a Suarez spot-kick, but the United goalkeeper was involved in another penalty incident that allowed the Sporting forward to find the net. United also had two goals ruled out, while Youri Tielemans was sent off late in the contest.

Despite the frustrating outcome, Pochettino was pleased with what he saw from his players.

The Argentine felt United controlled large periods of the first half but were disappointed to go into the break behind.

“The first half I think we controlled the game, I think we dominated. We were disappointed to finish the first half 1-0 down,” Pochettino said after the game.

Industry observers note that “The second half I think we started the way we want to play. That is the style, the character. That is the way we want to establish and feeling this way we can perform.”.

The United boss also made it clear that he was proud of the players despite the decisions and incidents that went against them.

“I’m so proud of my players. I think it was a very tough game. I liked the team during 90 minutes, in the way that we revealed personality and character.”.

Pochettino felt his side had been punished repeatedly in key moments.

Recent findings suggest that “In the second half, we recovered a lot of balls in the opposite half. We were aggressive and I think that is the way we want to play,” he added.

After the heavy defeat at Anfield, United showed a different level of fight in Lisbon. The draw will still feel like a missed opportunity for Manchester United and Pochettino. However, the Argentine manager believes his players are beginning to embrace the style of play he wants.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Birmingham City will head into the month of December as automatic promotion contenders in the Championship, having finally found their spark under Chris Davies.

A 10th-placed finish in the second tier last year, just 12 months after their 111-point haul in League One, was respectable enough, but there was always the scope for more to come from Davies' squad, and they're really showing it now.

Whilst Blues look to have depth all over the pitch, one area that they could look to bolster in the upcoming January transfer window is at the top end.

He had a slow start to life in the Midlands since his £6 million move from Djurgardens in January, but August Priske has finally come alive in the Championship.

The 22-year-old Dane found the back of the net just once from his 17 Championship appearances in the second half of 2025-26, but now acclimatised to English football, he's scored seven goals in 13 outings so far in the current campaign.

Priske has forged a good understanding with Jay Stansfield in the number 10 role, but his understudies have made little impact, with German veteran Marvin Ducksch and summer recruit Luis Vazquez both failing to fire off the bench.

It leaves Davies with a dilemma ahead of January - do City let one of the pair go and bring in a new striker to battle with Priske in the second half of the season as they push for the Premier League?

Blues may do just that, as reports have been emerging about a potential striker transfer target that is based in Spain.

According to a report from Ficherío, Sevilla forward Isaac Romero is on the club's radar ahead of the window's opening at the start of 2027, with the 26-year-old Spaniard growing frustrated with life at Los Nervionenses due to a lack of game-time this season.

It's claimed that Birmingham are already in contact with the agents of Romero in regards to a deal, and that a 'significant salary' has been put on the table for him to make the move to the second tier of English football - albeit it's also reported that Romero would like to stay at Sevilla if he gets more chances of minutes.

Romero was plucked from lower league Spanish outfit Antoniano in 2019, having started his youth career with Sevilla, making his first-team debut in 2024 for the club.

Starting in just four of his 11 La Liga appearances, Romero is behind Lucas Stassin and Robbie Ure in the pecking order, but he's scored more goals than the pair put together so far in the Spanish top flight, netting three times compared to Stassin and Ure's two goals combined.

If Birmingham make good progress with a move to sign Romero from Sevilla, then it could spark a departure from St. Andrew's - but not necessarily from their striker unit.

Reports from earlier in the week claim that Sevilla have an interest in signing Blues winger Carlos Vicente, who hasn't found his best form since signing from Alaves for £7 million last January.

Vicente worked under current Sevilla boss Luis Garcia Plaza whilst he was the manager of Alaves, and he's reportedly keen to re-unite with the 27-year-old just a year after he departed for England.

Industry observers note that would Isaac Romero be a good signing for Birmingham City? Comment below!

Pushed behind Patrick Roberts in the pecking order more often than not this season under Davies, Vicente could potentially play a part in a swap deal if all parties agree to it, but if initial reports are to be believed, it may be tough to get Romero out of Sevilla given he has a point to prove.

Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all.”.

It has been revealed that manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano has confirmed that the club intends to appeal the verdict. The statement from Guardiola comes to City’s defence despite him leaving the role this summer. He is still viewed as the man who built this era of success, even though he no longer sits in the dugout at the Etihad.

The Pep Guardiola Man City charges case matters just as much to Chelsea as it does to Manchester City themselves. Chelsea, along with Arsenal and Tottenham, are among the Premier League clubs directly affected by the outcome. For Chelsea supporters, the case is not just about points on a table. It touches on the integrity of seasons they competed in directly. That is why so many rivals are refusing to let the matter rest with a guilty verdict alone.

It has been revealed that manchester City’s appeal process is now the next stage in a case that has already run for nearly two years. Ferran Soriano has made clear the club will contest the findings. No date has been confirmed for when that appeal will be heard.

Sources indicate that until then, no points deductions, penalties or changes to past titles have been confirmed by the Premier League. Chelsea and their rivals will be watching the appeal timeline just as closely as they watched the original hearing. The final outcome could still be a long way off.
